record.original_question: Let Ω ⊂ Rd and consider a random N-point input in Ω. Can one obtain bounds of the form β1N^((d−1)/d) ≤ EH1(St) ≤ β2N^((d−1)/d) that distinguish the Steiner tree problem from the minimum spanning tree, the rectilinear Steiner tree, and the traveling salesperson problem? In the same random setting, what are good upper and lower bounds for the Steiner ratio?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d\ge 2$) be a bounded domain of positive Lebesgue measure (say the unit cube $[0,1]^d$), and let $X_1,\dots,X_N$ be i.i.d. uniformly distributed points in $\Omega$. For a finite set $T\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of "terminals", let $\mathrm{St}(T)$ denote a Euclidean Steiner minimum tree on $T$, i.e., a connected graph in $\mathbb{R}^d$ of minimum total Euclidean length that contains $T$ among its vertices (additional Steiner points are allowed). Let $\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{St}(T))$ denote its total length, and let $\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{MST}(T))$, $\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{RST}(T))$, $\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{TSP}(T))$ denote, respectively, the lengths of the Euclidean minimum spanning tree, the rectilinear Steiner minimum tree, and the optimal traveling salesperson tour on $T$. Write $\mathrm{St}_N := \mathrm{St}(\{X_1,\dots,X_N\})$.

(a) Determine constants $0<\beta_1(d)\le \beta_2(d)<\infty$ such that
$$\beta_1(d)\, N^{(d-1)/d} \;\le\; \mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{St}_N) \;\le\; \beta_2(d)\, N^{(d-1)/d}$$
for all sufficiently large $N$, with constants $\beta_1(d), \beta_2(d)$ that strictly distinguish the asymptotic behaviour of $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{St}_N)$ from the corresponding expectations $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{MST}_N)$, $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{RST}_N)$, and $\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{TSP}_N)$.

(b) Define the random Steiner ratio
$$\rho_N \;:=\; \frac{\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{St}_N)}{\mathbb{E}\,\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{MST}_N)}.$$
Provide the best possible explicit upper and lower bounds for $\liminf_{N\to\infty}\rho_N$ and $\limsup_{N\to\infty}\rho_N$ in dimension $d$.
artifact.status_search_result: Classical results of Beardwood–Halton–Hammersley (TSP) and Steele (MST/Steiner) show that for i.i.d. uniform points in a bounded region of $\mathbb{R}^d$, the expected lengths of the TSP, MST, and Steiner tree all scale like $N^{(d-1)/d}$ with positive constants. However, sharp constants that strictly separate the Steiner-tree constant from the MST, rectilinear, and TSP constants in general dimension are not known, and the asymptotic random Steiner ratio is not pinned down. No source found establishing the requested distinguishing bounds, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Steiner tree problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: General overview of Euclidean Steiner trees and the Steiner ratio; no sharp asymptotics for random point sets distinguishing MST/RST/TSP constants are reported.
status_evidence.claim: No published exact constants distinguishing the random Steiner-tree expectation from MST/RST/TSP expectations in general dimension.

status_evidence.title: The Steiner Ratio of Metric Spaces (Cieslik)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Steiner ratio in metric spaces; the random Steiner ratio in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is not determined.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp upper and lower bounds for the Steiner ratio in a random uniform setup are not established.
